market_brief: Nvidia cleared the bar after the close: $115.8B revenue, a Q4 guide of ~$130B and a $150B buyback lifted the stock ~2-4% after hours, and Kospi opened +2.6% back above 5,000. That came after a heavy Tuesday, with the S&P 500 -1.2%, Dow -1.8%, Euro Stoxx 50 -2.1% and DAX -2.1% on new US chip-export licence rules and Fed-hike bets, and the VIX up 12% to ~25.7. Rates and the dollar were calm (10Y 5.10%, -2bp; DXY ~103.5), Brent held near $92.8 despite a 5.3M-barrel API build, gold sat flat at ~$3,853 and bitcoin slipped to ~$63.8k (-13% w/w). Today's tests are UK CPI (3.6% expected), Fed minutes and Anthropic's IPO pricing, reportedly ~6-7x covered.
ai_brief: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with a 20% Astra price cut, but early power-user reaction was harsh and Artificial Analysis still ranks Claude Fable 5.2 ahead. Microsoft answered at Ignite with seven MAI models, including MAI Code 2 in Copilot. Nvidia's Vera Rubin ramp (~$20B in its first quarter) supports the AI-capex story, and finance-focused agent startup Model ML raised $250M at $1.5B.

items.headline: Nvidia beats: Q3 revenue $115.8B (+103% y/y), Q4 guide $127.4-132.6B, $150B more buyback
items.summary: EPS of $2.68 topped ~$2.47 consensus and data-center revenue hit $107.6B vs ~$101.9B expected; the FY2028 growth outlook was lifted to ~75%. Shares rose about 2-4.5% after hours from a $155.46 close.

items.headline: Update on Nvidia leadership: board says it will not reinstate Jensen Huang; Kress stays interim CEO
items.summary: New since yesterday: the board confirmed a permanent CEO search with CFO Colette Kress as interim chief, removing the guidance-withdrawal risk BofA had flagged. Gross margin was 74.8% and Vera Rubin shipped nearly $20B in its first production quarter.

items.headline: Wall Street falls for a fourth day: Dow -849 points, S&P 500 at lowest close since July
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell about 1% and the Dow 1.6% as chip curbs and Fed-hike bets weighed before Nvidia; the Nasdaq Composite briefly fell ~2% intraday. The VIX rose to about 25.5.

items.headline: US October retail sales +0.2% to $748.2B; industrial production -0.4%; import prices +1.1%
items.summary: Headline retail sales matched forecasts, with the control group reportedly up 0.6%, while factory output fell. Hot import prices add to the inflation worries behind December hike pricing.

items.headline: Fedspeak: Musalem floats up to four more hikes; Williams reportedly pushes back on an outsized move
items.summary: St. Louis Fed's Musalem said as many as four more increases may be needed before spring 2027, while NY Fed's Williams reportedly argued against a 50bp step. December hike odds sit near 95-100%, with the 10Y around 5.10%.

items.headline: Update: new US rule requires licences for advanced AI chip shipments to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil
items.summary: Follows yesterday's remote-access curb, now detailed with the country list; it hit European and Asian chip and AI-infrastructure names on Tuesday, with the DAX down ~2%.

items.headline: Kospi opens 2.6% higher back above 5,000 after Nvidia's outlook
items.summary: Seoul rebounded after four straight losses, with the Kospi at 5,098.82 early Wednesday and Kosdaq +2.3%; it had closed below 5,000 on Tuesday for the first time in about nine months.

items.headline: Update: Anthropic IPO reportedly ~6-7x oversubscribed ahead of pricing today
items.summary: The 825M-share offering (range $70-78, Nasdaq: ANT) reportedly drew around six to seven times the shares on offer despite the AI selloff; pricing is due Wednesday and trading Thursday.

items.headline: Prediction-market chatter: Steve Eisman reportedly unmoved by Anthropic's order book
items.summary: Per Benzinga's prediction-markets coverage, the 'Big Short' investor remains sceptical even as the deal is reported up to 7x covered; traders are also betting on ANT's day-one performance.

items.headline: Movers: SELLAS +156% on Phase 3 win; Red Cat -32% after pulling guidance; Home Depot names McPhail CEO
items.summary: SELLAS surged on positive REGAL survival data but slipped ~11% after hours on a proposed $150M offering. Energizer (+12.6%) and AECOM (+11.1%) rallied; Home Depot fell 2.5% as it said Richard McPhail becomes CEO on Nov 23.

items.headline: Crypto names downgraded: Galaxy Digital -10.5%, MARA -5% after analyst cuts
items.summary: Downgrades hit crypto brokers and miners as bitcoin slipped toward $64k, down ~13% on the week. Mizuho also downgraded Stanley Black & Decker, per separate reports.

items.headline: API reports 5.3M-barrel US crude build and 5.1M-barrel gasoline build; SPR drawn again
items.summary: Industry data for the week to Nov 13 showed large product builds while Cushing fell ~1.7M barrels; the SPR dropped 3.1M barrels to 276.4M. Brent holds near $92-93 as glut forecasts offset Hormuz disruption.

items.headline: UK October CPI due at 07:00 GMT; consensus 3.6% y/y vs 3.5% in September
items.summary: A rise would follow the BoE's Nov 5 hike to 4.00%; September core was 2.8% and services 3.7%. The FTSE 100 fell 1.8% on Tuesday.

items.headline: India set-up: Nifty eyes 25,500 resistance after two-day gain and record Bank Nifty
items.summary: Analysts cite 25,200 support and 25,500 resistance after Tuesday's 25,387 close; Nvidia's beat and the Asia rebound could test the India-over-AI rotation seen this week.

items.headline: Next 48h: UK CPI, Fed minutes, EIA stocks and Anthropic pricing (Wed); ANT debut and GTA VI launch (Thu)
items.summary: Fed minutes will be read for how many hikes officials see; ANT's first trade is the next test for AI sentiment after Nvidia. APEC meetings also run this week.

items.headline: OpenAI ships GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol; Astra API price cut 20% to $8/$40 per M tokens
items.summary: Both models offer ~1M-token context and are live in ChatGPT, Codex and the API; Sol stays at $2/$10. OpenAI cites 78.3% on Agents' Last Exam for Astra and an ultrafast tier for Pro users.

items.headline: GPT-6.2 draws a harsh first reaction from power users on X
items.summary: Several prominent developers called the release unusable or uneven, while Artificial Analysis ranked Astra second on its index behind Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2.

items.headline: GPT-6.2 models cross OpenAI's 'Critical' cybersecurity threshold and ship with tighter safeguards
items.summary: OpenAI says both new models meet its highest cyber-capability tier under its preparedness framework, triggering added restrictions on misuse.

items.headline: Microsoft launches seven MAI models at Ignite, including MAI Code 2 and a speech-to-speech model
items.summary: MAI Code 2 is in GitHub Copilot and claimed at ~98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's quality for ~40% of the price; MAI Cyber 2 Flash costs $0.10/$0.50 per M tokens. Microsoft also says its Maia 200 accelerator is in production.

items.headline: Nvidia's quarter signals AI capex intact: Vera Rubin nears $20B in first production quarter
items.summary: Data-center revenue of $107.6B and a Q4 guide above estimates eased fears of an AI-spending slowdown; Nvidia also disclosed $390B of purchase commitments.

items.headline: Model ML raises $250M at $1.5B for AI agents that work inside Excel and PowerPoint
items.summary: General Atlantic and QED co-led the round for the finance-and-consulting agent startup, which says revenue is split across consultancies, banks and asset managers.

items.headline: Nvidia-backed Genesis AI reportedly raises funds at a $3.5B valuation
items.summary: Bloomberg reports the physical-AI/robotics model developer closed a new round, extending this week's run of large robotics financings.

items.headline: Google begins replacing Gemini 'Gems' with slash-command 'skills' from Nov 17
items.summary: Existing Gems migrate automatically; AI Pro and Ultra subscribers will be able to build their own skills via the Gemini Spark tab.
